name: pharos-repoqa
labeling: Phase 2 Repo QA (LongMemEval-style): questions about a repository's history, conventions and procedures that a code index alone answers poorly. Written by hand from git history and source at each repository's utility_v1 cutoff commit (C0), before any Phase 2 memory existed. Each answer is scored against its key_facts: 'correct' when every key fact is stated, 'partial' when at least one is, 'wrong' otherwise; a confident claim that contradicts a key fact counts as wrong. Abstention questions are correct when the answer says the repository does not do the thing.

questions.question: How does click deprecate a public name or attribute before removing it?
questions.answer: It keeps the old name working and calls warnings.warn with a DeprecationWarning and stacklevel=2, with a message of the form "'X' is deprecated and will be removed in Click 9.0. Use 'Y' instead." Module-level names are served through __getattr__ in click/__init__.py.
key_facts: message says it will be removed in Click 9.0

questions.question: Where are changelog entries written in click, and how is an entry formatted?
questions.answer: In CHANGES.md (Markdown; it was CHANGES.rst until June 2026), under a '## Version X.Y.Z' heading marked 'Unreleased' or 'Released <date>'. Each entry is a bullet that ends with {issue}`N` and/or {pr}`N` references.
key_facts: a section per version, Unreleased or Released with a date

questions.question: When did click stop using colorama, and what does it rely on instead on Windows?
questions.answer: Colorama was removed in May 2026 (PR #3505) for the 8.5.0 release. Supported Windows versions enable ANSI terminal styles by default, so click no longer needs colorama.

questions.question: When someone changes src/click/core.py, which other files usually change in the same commit?
questions.answer: Most often the changelog (CHANGES.rst, now CHANGES.md) and tests/test_options.py; next src/click/types.py, src/click/decorators.py, tests/test_commands.py and tests/test_arguments.py.
evidence: git log of the 300 latest non-merge commits touching src/click/core.py before C0: CHANGES.rst 131, tests/test_options.py 64, src/click/types.py 40

questions.question: Do click's library modules use postponed evaluation of annotations?
questions.answer: Yes: every module under src/click starts with 'from __future__ import annotations', and the library is fully type-annotated.
key_facts: from __future__ import annotations in every module
evidence: all 17 .py files under src/click at C0

questions.question: How do click docstrings record that an API changed or was added in a given version?
questions.answer: With Sphinx directives inside the docstring: '.. versionchanged:: X.Y' and '.. versionadded:: X.Y' (core.py alone has 76 of them).

questions.question: How do bug fixes and new features flow between click's branches?
questions.answer: Bug fixes for the current release line go to the 'stable' branch, which is then merged into 'main' ('Merge stable into main'); new features land on main.
key_facts: fixes go to the stable branch
evidence: first-parent merges of stable into main, e.g. 240603f

questions.question: Which asyncio integration does click provide for writing async command callbacks?
questions.answer: None: click's library code has no asyncio or async support; callbacks are synchronous.
key_facts: click has no built-in async/asyncio support
evidence: git grep -i async src at C0: no matches

questions.question: What happened to the SSLContext caching that requests introduced in 2.32.0?
questions.answer: It was reverted in 2.32.5 (2025-08-18): it created a new class of issues across many use cases, and the team judged its maintenance unsustainable in that form.
key_facts: because it caused a new class of issues / was unsustainable to maintain

questions.question: Where is the requests version number defined, and how does packaging pick it up?
questions.answer: In src/requests/__version__.py as __version__ (alongside __build__ and other metadata); pyproject.toml declares the version dynamic and reads it with [tool.setuptools.dynamic] version = {attr = "requests.__version__.__version__"}.
key_facts: pyproject dynamic version read from that attribute

questions.question: How is the requests changelog organised?
questions.answer: HISTORY.md ('Release History'), newest first, starting with a 'dev' section for unreleased changes. Each release heading is 'X.Y.Z (YYYY-MM-DD)' with bold groups such as **Bugfixes**, **Improvements**, **Deprecations** and **Security**.
key_facts: bold groups such as Bugfixes / Improvements / Deprecations / Security

questions.question: Which Python versions has requests dropped most recently, and when?
questions.answer: Python 3.8 was dropped in 2.32.5 (August 2025). Python 3.9 was dropped on the development branch in February 2026 (PR #7196), so requires-python is now >=3.10.

questions.question: Which CVE did requests 2.32.4 fix, and what was the problem?
questions.answer: CVE-2024-47081: a maliciously crafted URL together with a trusted environment could make requests retrieve netrc credentials for the wrong host.
key_facts: netrc credentials leaked for the wrong host via a crafted URL

questions.question: When sessions.py changes in requests, which other files usually change with it?
questions.answer: models.py most often, then the main test file (tests/test_requests.py, earlier test_requests.py at the root), utils.py and adapters.py.
evidence: git log of the 200 latest non-merge commits touching sessions.py before C0: models.py 33, tests/test_requests.py 29, utils.py 22, adapters.py 19

questions.question: When did requests move its package into a src/ directory?
questions.answer: In August 2023, PR #6506 ('Move to src directory'); before that the package lived in requests/ at the repository root.

questions.question: What header does every cobra Go source file start with?
questions.answer: '// Copyright 2013-2023 The Cobra Authors' followed by the Apache License, Version 2.0 notice.

questions.question: When was ActiveHelp added to cobra?
questions.answer: In June 2022, PR #1482 ('Add Active Help support'), which added active_help.go.

questions.question: Where does cobra keep its user-facing documentation, such as the shell completion guides?
questions.answer: Under site/content/ (for example site/content/completions/bash.md and site/content/active_help.md); the Markdown docs were moved there in June 2023 (PR #1428).

questions.question: How is the environment variable that controls ActiveHelp for a program named, and how can it be disabled globally?
questions.answer: <PROGRAM>_ACTIVE_HELP, where <PROGRAM> is the root command's name upper-cased with every non-ASCII-alphanumeric character replaced by '_'. Setting COBRA_ACTIVE_HELP=0 disables it for all programs.
key_facts: <PROGRAM>_ACTIVE_HELP from the upper-cased root command name

questions.question: When completions.go changes in cobra, which other files usually change with it?
questions.answer: completions_test.go most often, then command.go, then the per-shell scripts (bash_completions.go, zsh_completions.go, fish_completions.go, powershell_completions.go, bash_completionsV2.go).
evidence: git log of the 150 latest non-merge commits touching completions.go before C0: completions_test.go 18, command.go 13

questions.question: What does cobra ask contributors to run before submitting a pull request?
questions.answer: The tests ('go test ./...' or 'make test') and 'make all', which checks gofmt formatting and runs the tests; 'make lint' runs golangci-lint. Contributors also sign a CLA.

questions.question: Which configuration-file formats does cobra itself read for command defaults?
questions.answer: None: cobra does not read configuration files (that is viper's job). Its YAML dependency is only used to generate YAML documentation in doc/.
key_facts: cobra does not read config files
evidence: yaml is imported only by doc/yaml_docs.go, doc/util.go and tests

questions.question: How are curl commit messages formatted?
questions.answer: Subject 'area: short description' (for example 'urlapi: ...', 'tool_progress: ...'), then an explanatory body, then trailers: almost always 'Closes #NNNNN', sometimes 'Reported-by:', 'Follow-up to <sha>' or 'Fixes #N'.
evidence: the 30 commits before C0: 26 carry a Closes trailer

questions.question: What is the maximum line width for curl source code, and what enforces it?
questions.answer: 79 columns, stated in docs/internals/CODE_STYLE.md and enforced by scripts/checksrc.pl.

questions.question: How are function names prefixed in curl, depending on who may call them?
questions.answer: Public libcurl API functions start with 'curl_' (lowercase). Library-global functions that are not exported start with 'Curl_'. Functions shared by the library, the tool and the tests start with 'curlx_'. Functions used in one file are static with lowercase names.
key_facts: curlx_ for functions shared with the tool/tests

questions.question: Which files does adding a new libcurl option with a matching command-line option touch in curl?
questions.answer: Library: include/curl/curl.h (the CURLOPT), lib/setopt.c, lib/urldata.h, lib/easyoptions.c, docs/libcurl/opts/CURLOPT_<NAME>.md plus docs/libcurl/opts/Makefile.inc, docs/libcurl/symbols-in-versions and docs/libcurl/curl_easy_setopt.md. Tool: docs/cmdline-opts/<option>.md plus its Makefile.inc, src/tool_getparam.c and .h, src/tool_cfgable.h, src/tool_listhelp.c, src/tool_operate.c, and docs/options-in-versions.

questions.question: Which C library functions are banned in curl's sources, and what checks this?
questions.answer: scripts/checksrc.pl bans many, including sprintf, vsprintf, strcpy, strcat, strncpy, strtok, gets, atoi, atol, strtol, printf and the raw allocators malloc, calloc, realloc, free and strdup (curl uses its curlx_ wrappers such as curlx_malloc).
key_facts: raw malloc/free are banned in favour of curlx_ wrappers

questions.question: When lib/setopt.c changes, which other files usually change with it?
questions.answer: lib/urldata.h and lib/url.c most often, then lib/http.c, TLS backends such as lib/vtls/openssl.c, and lib/ftp.c.
evidence: git log of the 150 latest non-merge commits touching lib/setopt.c before C0: urldata.h 62, url.c 60, http.c 42

questions.question: When did curl add HTTP Message Signatures, and which libcurl options came with it?
questions.answer: In July 2026 (commit a55731050e, 'httpsig: add RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures support'). It added CURLOPT_HTTPSIG_ALGORITHM, CURLOPT_HTTPSIG_HEADERS, CURLOPT_HTTPSIG_KEY and CURLOPT_HTTPSIG_KEYID, with --httpsig-* command-line options, as an experimental feature.

questions.question: What does curl use for debug-time assertions?
questions.answer: The DEBUGASSERT() macro (over 1,200 uses in lib/); plain assert() is banned by checksrc.
